name: sol_hmt_2
description: Merkle-tree claim function omits msg.sender validation against leaf address
question: The source file in `source` implements a claim() function that verifies a Merkle proof against a leaf encoding an address and amount, but does not check that msg.sender equals (or is authorized by) that leaf address, allowing any caller who obtains a valid proof to claim funds or benefits intended for a different address, excluding cases where the leaf intentionally omits an address (e.g., bearer-style claims) or where the recipient address is separately validated via another mechanism such as a signature.
criteria: claim(bytes32[] proof, address account, uint256 amount) verifies MerkleProof.verify(proof, root, leaf) and transfers tokens to account without requiring msg.sender == account
claimReward(uint256 index, address user, uint256 amount, bytes32[] proof) checks the Merkle proof matching (index, user, amount) but pays out to user regardless of who calls the function
distribute() computes leaf = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(recipient, amount)), validates it against the Merkle root, then sends funds to recipient without comparing recipient to msg.sender
airdropClaim(bytes32[] calldata merkleProof, address claimer, uint256 amount) marks claimer as claimed and transfers tokens to claimer with no check that msg.sender equals claimer
